A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same operator deep smoothing work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original smoothing experiments on intraday S&P 500 data, cross-index evaluations in Table 1, and interpolation/extrapolation backtests in Table 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds hyperparameter ablations, runtime measurements, and results on synthetic SSVI data.

M1.justification: The interpolating GNO architecture, loss components, default weights, and 102529-parameter configuration remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 expands the existing neighborhood-construction description; the new ablations vary existing components without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds evaluation on a synthetic SSVI-generated surface. Intraday S&P 500 and end-of-day SPX, NDX, DJX, and RUT coverage remains. Removing the RUT example plot does not remove RUT evaluation, which survives in Table 1.

E2.justification: The principal SVI and Ackerer et al. Deep Smoothing comparisons remain. However, v2's Figure 16 provides a qualitative SVI-versus-OpDS comparison for RUT that v3 omits. The new SSVI experiment uses SSVI as a data generator, not an additional fitted baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces sequential 20-epoch neighborhood-size sweeps, separate 20-epoch arbitrage-weight experiments, synthetic evaluation on input and dense output grids, and CPU/GPU timing with 897 inputs and 2500 outputs. The original data splits, 500-epoch training schedule, metrics, and monthly finetuning protocol remain.

E4.justification: New Appendices C.6–C.7 test neighborhood-size sensitivity and the accuracy/arbitrage tradeoff from penalty weighting. C.8–C.9 add input-evolution and computational-scaling analyses, while D.4 adds a synthetic case study. These substantially expand the analyses beyond v2; the RUT example is removed.

E5.justification: Table 2 replaces minimum and maximum statistics with first and 99th percentiles. Existing mean, standard-deviation, and quartile reporting and the 25-repetition backtest remain. The new ablation tables extend descriptive reporting without adding seed-based uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include hyperparameter sensitivities, CPU/GPU timings of 336/16.7 ms at K=50, and synthetic MAPE values of 2.01% and 2.42%. Table 2 revises validation values, including mean fitting loss from 0.022 to 0.0182, without explaining the revision. Tables 1 and 3–5 retain their values. Figure 2 changes example dates, and the RUT example results disappear.

T1.justification: Equation 3 changes the implied-density denominator from v to v sqrt(tau). Appendix C.9 adds a derivation of O(J(n_in+n_out)K) forward-pass complexity. The volatility-validation and neural-operator theorems remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: discretization-invariant smoothing with one trained operator, improved fitting over SVI, competitiveness with Deep Smoothing, and cross-index generalization. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of neighborhood locality, accuracy/computation tradeoffs, and possible monotonicity overfitting. It also introduces applicability limits concerning lower-frequency training data and sub-millisecond trading, including approximately 100 ms graph-construction overhead. These extend v2's limitations concerning interpretability and dimensionality reduction.

D1.justification: v3 details neighborhood subsampling, synthetic-data parameters and grids, and computational overhead. Its new reproducibility statement explains workflows, proprietary-data restrictions, and omitted intermediate artifacts beyond v2's brief code/weights disclosures. Reported training time changes from approximately 200 to 250 hours on the same GPU; the stated epoch budget is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lind and Gatheral (2023) as the source of the synthetic SSVI formulation and parameter choices. The existing literature review, comparator positioning, and novelty claims otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and ordering remain, with localized copyediting, expanded neighborhood explanations, and new Reproducibility and Ethics statements. Author order and Gonon's affiliation also change. This is not a wholesale rewrite of the existing paper.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout, adds Tables 6–10 and graph-construction, option-trajectory, option-count, and synthetic-result figures, and redraws Figure 2. Captions and legends are revised, and the RUT figure is removed. Most other appendix plots are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's manually justified hyperparameters and brief resource disclosures, v3 provides useful sensitivity tests, measured runtime, clearer implementation information, and explicit practical limitations. These improve assessment and reproducibility. However, checkpoint-based ablations, particularly the sequential K sweep, and unexplained Table 2 revisions limit the strength of the additional evidence; the main benchmark conclusions remain unchanged.
